claim: CoSMO comprises two non-mating engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains: L-H+ requires lysine (L) and pays a fitness cost to overproduce hypoxanthine (H, an adenine derivative), while H-L+ requires hypoxanthine and pays a fitness cost to overproduce lysine.
source: CoSMO comprises two non-mating engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains: L-H+ requires lysine (L) and pays a fitness cost to overproduce hypoxanthine (H, an adenine derivative) (Waite and Shou, 2012; Hart et al., 2019a), while H-L+ requires hypoxanthine and pays a fitness cost to overproduce lysine (Hart et al., 2019b; Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text and supported by citations to previous work (Waite and Shou, 2012; Hart et al., 2019a; Hart et al., 2019b) and reference to Figure 1A.

claim: Overproduced metabolites are released into the environment by live cells, allowing the two strains to feed each other.
source: Overproduced metabolites are released into the environment by live cells (Hart et al., 2019a), allowing the two strains to feed each other.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Hart et al., 2019a.

claim: CoSMO models the metabolic cooperation between certain gut microbial species and between legumes and rhizobia, as well as other mutualisms.
source: CoSMO models the metabolic cooperation between certain gut microbial species (Rakoff-Nahoum et al., 2016) and between legumes and rhizobia (Schubert, 1986), as well as other mutualisms (Beliaev et al., 2014; Helliwell et al., 2011; Carini et al., 2014; Rodionova et al., 2015; Zengler and Zaramela, 2018; Jiang et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by multiple citations to literature.

claim: In CoSMO, exchanged metabolites are costly to produce.
source: Similar to natural systems, in CoSMO exchanged metabolites are costly to produce (Waite and Shou, 2012; Hart et al., 2019a), and cooperation can transition to competition when the exchanged metabolites are externally supplied (Momeni et al., 2013b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Waite and Shou, 2012 and Hart et al., 2019a.

claim: In CoSMO, cooperation can transition to competition when the exchanged metabolites are externally supplied.
source: Similar to natural systems, in CoSMO exchanged metabolites are costly to produce (Waite and Shou, 2012; Hart et al., 2019a), and cooperation can transition to competition when the exchanged metabolites are externally supplied (Momeni et al., 2013b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Momeni et al., 2013b.

claim: Nine independent lines of CoSMO were allowed to evolve for over 100 generations in a well-mixed environment by performing periodic dilutions.
source: In our previous work, we allowed nine independent lines of CoSMO to evolve for over 100 generations in a well-mixed environment by performing periodic dilutions (Hart et al., 2019a; Shou et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Hart et al., 2019a and Shou et al., 2007.

claim: Throughout evolution, the two cooperating strains coexisted due to their metabolic co-dependence.
source: Throughout evolution, the two cooperating strains coexisted due to their metabolic co-dependence (Momeni et al., 2013b; Shou et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Momeni et al., 2013b and Shou et al., 2007.

claim: All characterized mutants isolated from CoSMO displayed self-serving phenotypic changes.
source: Indeed, all characterized mutants isolated from CoSMO displayed self-serving phenotypic changes (e.g. improved affinity for partner-supplied metabolites; Waite and Shou, 2012; Hart et al., 2019a; Hart et al., 2019b), outcompeting their ancestor in community-like environments.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Waite and Shou, 2012; Hart et al., 2019a; Hart et al., 2019b.

claim: A pleiotropic win-win mutation which is both self-serving and partner-serving was identified in CoSMO.
source: Here, we report the identification of a pleiotropic win-win mutation which is both self-serving and partner-serving.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: The win-win mutation also arose in the absence of the cooperative partner.
source: This win-win mutation also arose in the absence of the cooperative partner.
evidence: The claim is directly stated in the text.

claim: Cooperation-promoting win-win mutations can arise in a community without any evolutionary history of cooperation and in environments unfavorable to cooperation.
source: Thus, cooperation-promoting win-win mutations can arise in a community without any evolutionary history of cooperation and in environments unfavorable to cooperation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a conclusion from the study's findings.

claim: Pre-existing pleiotropy can stabilize nascent cooperation in natural communities.
source: Our work suggests the possibility that pre-existing pleiotropy can stabilize nascent cooperation in natural communities.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a suggestion based on the study's findings.

claim: A win-win mutation is defined as a single mutation that directly promotes the fitness of self (self-serving) and the fitness of partner (partner-serving).
source: A win-win mutation is defined as a single mutation (e.g., a point mutation, a translocation, a chromosome duplication) that directly promotes the fitness of self (self-serving) and the fitness of partner (partner-serving).
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a definition in the text.

claim: A mutation in genotype A exerts a direct fitness effect on genotype B if the mutation can alter the growth rate of B even if the biomass of A is fixed.
source: To define 'direct' here, we adapt the framework from Chapter 10 of Peters et al., 2017: A mutation in genotype A exerts a direct fitness effect on genotype B if the mutation can alter the growth rate of B even if the biomass of A is fixed (Hart et al., 2019b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Peters et al., 2017 and Hart et al., 2019b.

claim: For L-H+, a self-serving mutation should improve the growth rate of self by, for example, increasing cell's affinity for lysine.
source: For L-H+, a self-serving mutation should improve the growth rate of self by, for example, increasing cell's affinity for lysine (Figure 1B, orange).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and references Figure 1B.

claim: A partner-serving mutation in L-H+ should increase the hypoxanthine supply rate per L-H+ biomass.
source: A partner-serving mutation should improve the growth rate of partner at a fixed self biomass. Since the partner requires hypoxanthine, a partner-serving mutation in L-H+ should increase the hypoxanthine supply rate per L-H+ biomass.
evidence: The claim is directly stated based on logical reasoning about partner requirements.

claim: The partner-serving phenotype of L-H+ translates to hypoxanthine supply rate per lysine consumption, or equivalently, hypoxanthine release rate per cell (rH) normalized by the amount of lysine consumed to make a cell (cL).
source: Since the biomass of L-H+ is linked to lysine consumption, the partner-serving phenotype of L-H+ translates to hypoxanthine supply rate per lysine consumption, or equivalently, hypoxanthine release rate per cell (rH) normalized by the amount of lysine consumed to make a cell (cL) (Hart et al., 2019b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Hart et al., 2019b.

claim: The ratio rH/cL is called 'H-L exchange ratio', which can be interpreted as the yield coefficient while converting lysine consumption to hypoxanthine release.
source: We call this ratio rH/cL 'H-L exchange ratio' (Figure 1B, purple), which can be interpreted as the yield coefficient while converting lysine consumption to hypoxanthine release.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and references Figure 1B.

claim: Nearly every sequenced L-H+ clone from CoSMO harbored one or more of the following mutations: ecm21, rsp5, and duplication of chromosome 14 (DISOMY14).
source: We randomly isolated evolved L-H+ colonies from CoSMO and subjected them to whole-genome sequencing. Nearly every sequenced clone harbored one or more of the following mutations: ecm21, rsp5, and duplication of chromosome 14 (DISOMY14) (Table 1, top), consistent with our earlier studies (Waite and Shou, 2012; Hart et al., 2019a; Hart et al., 2019b; Green et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations and reference to Table 1.

claim: Mutations in RSP5 mostly involved point mutations, while mutations in ECM21 mostly involved premature stop codons and frameshift mutations.
source: Mutations in RSP5, an essential gene, mostly involved point mutations (e.g., rsp5(P772L)), while mutations in ECM21 mostly involved premature stop codons and frameshift mutations (Table 1, top; Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by references to Table 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Similar mutations to those found in CoSMO also repeatedly arose when L-H+ evolved as a monoculture in lysine-limited chemostats.
source: Similar mutations also repeatedly arose when L-H+ evolved as a monoculture in lysine-limited chemostats (Table 1, bottom), suggesting that these mutations emerged independently of the partner.
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Table 1.

claim: The mutations in L-H+ emerged independently of the partner.
source: Similar mutations also repeatedly arose when L-H+ evolved as a monoculture in lysine-limited chemostats (Table 1, bottom), suggesting that these mutations emerged independently of the partner.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a suggestion based on the observation that mutations arose in monocultures.

claim: Evolved L-H+ clones could form microcolonies on low-lysine plates where the ancestor failed to grow.
source: Evolved L-H+ clones are known to display a self-serving phenotype: they could form microcolonies on low-lysine plates where the ancestor failed to grow (Waite and Shou, 2012; Hart et al., 2019b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by citations to Waite and Shou, 2012 and Hart et al., 2019b.

claim: Under lysine limitation characteristic of the CoSMO environment, evolved L-H+ clones containing an ecm21 or rsp5 mutation grew faster than a DISOMY14 strain, which grew faster than the ancestor.
source: Under lysine limitation characteristic of the CoSMO environment (Figure 2A, 'Comm. environ.'), evolved L-H+ clones containing an ecm21 or rsp5 mutation grew faster than a DISOMY14 strain which, as we showed previously, grew faster than the ancestor (Hart et al., 2019b).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2A and a citation to Hart et al., 2019b.

claim: An engineered ecm21Δ or rsp5(P772L) mutation was sufficient to confer the self-serving phenotype.
source: An engineered ecm21Δ or rsp5(P772L) mutation was sufficient to confer the self-serving phenotype (Figure 2A).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2A.

claim: In competition experiments in lysine-limited chemostats (8 hr doubling time), ecm21Δ rapidly outcompeted ancestral cells since ecm21Δ grew 4.4 times as fast as the ancestor.
source: In competition experiments in lysine-limited chemostats (8 hr doubling time), ecm21Δ rapidly outcompeted ancestral cells since ecm21Δ grew 4.4 times as fast as the ancestor (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In high lysine, Lyp1-GFP was localized to both cell membrane and vacuole in ancestral and ecm21 cells, but localized to the cell membrane in rsp5 cells.
source: In high lysine, Lyp1-GFP was localized to both cell membrane and vacuole in ancestral and ecm21 cells, but localized to the cell membrane in rsp5 cells (Figure 2B, top row).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Lyp1 localization was normal in ecm21 but not in rsp5, consistent with the notion that at high lysine concentrations, Lyp1 is targeted for ubiquitination by Rsp5 through the Art1 instead of the Ecm21 adaptor.
source: Thus, Lyp1 localization was normal in ecm21 but not in rsp5, consistent with the notion that at high lysine concentrations, Lyp1 is targeted for ubiquitination by Rsp5 through the Art1 instead of the Ecm21 adaptor (Lin et al., 2008).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Lin et al., 2008.

claim: When ancestral L-H+ was incubated in low lysine, Lyp1-GFP was initially localized on the cell membrane to facilitate lysine uptake, but later targeted to the vacuole for degradation and recycling.
source: When ancestral L-H+ was incubated in low lysine, Lyp1-GFP was initially localized on the cell membrane to facilitate lysine uptake, but later targeted to the vacuole for degradation and recycling (Jones et al., 2012; Figure 2B, left column middle and bottom panels).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by a citation to Jones et al., 2012 and reference to Figure 2B.

claim: In both ecm21Δ and rsp5(P772L) mutants, Lyp1-GFP was stabilized on cell membrane during prolonged lysine limitation.
source: However, in both ecm21Δ and rsp5(P772L) mutants, Lyp1-GFP was stabilized on cell membrane during prolonged lysine limitation (Figure 2B, center and right columns bottom panels).
evidence: The claim is directly stated and supported by reference to Figure 2B.

claim: Stabilization of Lyp1-GFP on cell membrane in ecm21Δ and rsp5(P772L) mutants could allow mutants to grow faster than the ancestor during lysine limitation.
source: This could allow mutants to grow faster than the ancestor during lysine limitation.
evidence: The claim is directly stated as a possible explanation.

source: Specifically, at the same dilution rate (corresponding to 6 hr doubling), the steady state hypoxanthine concentration was the highest in ecm21∆, and lower in the ancestor, DISOMY14 (Hart et al., 2019b), and rsp5(P772L) (Figure 3A).

claim: The same steady state growth rate was achieved by the two cooperating strains in CoSMO.
source: The same steady state growth rate was also achieved by the two cooperating strains (Hart et al., 2019b).

source: Compared to the ancestor, ecm21∆ indeed sped up the steady state growth rate of CoSMO and of partner H-L+ (Figure 4B).

source: The partner-serving phenotype of ecm21∆ can be explained by the increased hypoxanthine release rate per lysine consumption, rather than the evolution of any new metabolic interactions.

claim: All evolved L-H+ clones displayed self-serving phenotypes, achieving a higher growth rate than the ancestor in low lysine presumably by stabilizing the lysine permease Lyp1 on cell membrane.
